benchmark.alternative_consumption_note: Ofgem's medium Typical Domestic Consumption Value for single-rate electricity is 2,500 kWh from 1 July 2026 (Ofgem, Review of typical domestic consumption values: decision, May 2026; was 2,700). The bill at this and the other archetype volumes is the standing charge plus the unit rate times consumption, on the declared charge_basis (item G6).
benchmark.period_alignment_note: Calendar 2030, the year the model dispatches (user decision, 28 Sep 2026). Model lines are calendar 2030 by construction. Every sourced external declares period_basis: calendar_year (the Capacity Market takes half of each delivery year), calendar_blend (0.25 x FY2029/30 + 0.75 x FY2030/31, each fiscal year deflated at its own midpoint: TNUoS, FiT, WHD), period_average (remaining CCS, a 2028/29-2030/31 average) or held_flat_real (a sourced earlier value held flat in real terms, with its source_period). The RO counts each station for the share of calendar 2030 it is accredited. The projector refuses a line without a basis.
benchmark.payment_method_scope: A direct-debit household (Ofgem's 'other payment method' allowances), which pays Ofgem's levelisation between payment methods (Annex 9 v1.11: +3.48 a year in Oct-Dec 2026, GB mean), carried in supplier_costs_and_margin (user decision, 6 Oct 2026, F18). A standard-credit customer would pay about GBP81 more at 3,100 kWh.

currency_rebasing.index: ONS CPIH annual average, all items, 2015=100

cfd_strike_indexation.index: ONS CPI annual average, all items, 2015=100 (CDID D7BT)
cfd_strike_indexation.validation: DESNZ publishes AR7 offshore wind at GBP65.45 (2012 prices) and GBP91.20 (2024 prices), a ratio of 1.39343, and AR7a onshore at 51.85/72.24 = 1.39325 and solar at 46.82/65.23 = 1.39321. This CPI annual-average ratio of 1.393340 reproduces the department's own published conversion, so the indexation basis is not an assumption made here.
cfd_strike_indexation.note: CfD strikes are indexed annually under the contract terms using a CPI reference that need not equal the annual average used for a price-basis conversion. This factor is the published 2012-to-2024 price-basis conversion, which is what is needed to state strikes on the model's 2024 basis; it is not the contractual within-year indexation mechanic.

direct_fuel.formula: (Ofgem 70/30 baseload/peak blend of the PyPSA hourly clearing prices per quarter, weighted by household volume) x (1 + Ofgem shaping allowances) + Ofgem-named procurement allowances, x 3.1 MWh, rebased to GBP real 2025

domestic_shaping.method: Weight the hourly PyPSA clearing price by relative domestic demand instead of total system load. The difference between the two weightings is reported as an explicit shaping_adjustment row so the reader can see what shaping is worth.
domestic_shaping.source: Ofgem default tariff cap model Annex 2 base/peak demand allocation for the 2020 cap periods, pinned at data/market/ofgem_price_cap/2020_annual/hedged_wholesale_inputs.csv
domestic_shaping.profile_year_note: The CP30 monthly runs use renewables_year 2013 and demand_year 2013, not 2020 as an earlier version of this note stated. The 2020 cap periods are the vintage of Ofgem's base/peak allocation, which is the only structure this profile carries (weekday and local hour); it has no weather or calendar-year content, so the mismatch between 2013 model weather and the 2020 cap vintage has no effect on the shaping value. The profile is mapped onto 2030 snapshots by day-of-week and local hour.

procurement_bridge.method: Ofgem-named procurement allowances applied to the PyPSA domestic-profile energy cost. Each allowance is an observed 2020 intensity relative to the delivery price, carried forward as an explicit assumption. Shaping is its own row (direct_fuel.shaping: the Ofgem cap rule), not one of these allowances. The supplier imbalance allowance is included (item D4(d), 26 Sep 2026): an earlier version excluded it as 'recovered through BSUoS', which is wrong, because BSUoS recovers NESO's balancing actions while a supplier's own imbalance is cash-out settled through Elexon and is priced into its tariff.
procurement_bridge.source: data/market/ofgem_price_cap/2020_annual/hedged_wholesale_inputs.csv, delivery-day-weighted across the three 2020 cap periods (91 / 183 / 92 days)
procurement_bridge.price_year_note: These are dimensionless intensities relative to the delivery price, not cash amounts, so they need no rebasing. Applying them to a rebased energy cost yields an allowance already on the report basis.
procurement_bridge.rate_composition_note: User decision, 6 Oct 2026 (F18): Ofgem's direct-fuel formula exactly. Annex 2 tab 1b adds the rates together on the index, index x (1 + shaping + transaction + day-ahead re-hedging + imbalance + additional risk), and applies losses after all of them; each bill line is its own share. The bill used to apply the four hedging rates to the shaped price (+0.19 GBP) and losses to energy plus shaping only (-0.43 GBP). For electricity Ofgem's 1% is 'additional risk'; there is no separate basis-risk allowance (the line keeps its id, procurement_additional_risk_and_basis).

losses.formula: index x (1 + sum of rates) x (loss_multiplier - 1)
losses.source: Ofgem default tariff cap, Annex 2 v1.30 (Oct-Dec 2026), tab '3c Electricity losses', row 'Single-Rate Metering Arrangement, Average' (GB average)
losses.note: User decision, 6 Oct 2026 (F18): the household's current single-rate loss factor, the one every GSP-rate line carries (household_loss_factor in the recovery file; the projector checks they are equal). It replaces the delivery-weighted 2020 GB-average multiplier (1.0919), which also stood in for the system's metered-supply factor.

imbalance.source: Ofgem default tariff cap, Annex 2 (wholesale) tab '3a Allowances', electricity 'Imbalance' uplift, 1.3104% in all three 2020 cap periods (data/market/ofgem_price_cap/2020_source/2020_10_to_2020_03_annex_2_wholesale_v1.6.xlsx; data/market/ofgem_price_cap/2020_annual/hedged_wholesale_inputs.csv, column imbalance_rate)
imbalance.note: Supplier cash-out exposure (item D4(d)). A dimensionless intensity on the delivery price, so no rebasing. It does not overlap BSUoS: NESO's energy-imbalance actions are in the BSUoS lines, the supplier's imbalance charges are paid to Elexon.

forward_premium.backwardation_reference: Ofgem's backwardation allowance in the latest cap (Oct-Dec 2026): about 28 GBP a year at 3,100 kWh, GB average, Oct-Dec 2026 money (Annex 2 v1.30, tab 1a Wholesale allowance, rows 48-61, scaled from the 2,500 kWh typical value). Its transitional component changes sign from quarter to quarter (tab 8a(i): -8.2, +4.2, -0.1, -14.5 for Eastern over Q1 to Q4 2026). Shown for size only; the central case stays at zero (user decision, 6 Oct 2026) and the +5% and +10% sensitivities bracket it.
forward_premium.note: No forward premium on modelled spot in the central case: Ofgem's cap carries only its named allowances (including the 1% additional risk allowance, here in additional_risk_and_basis) and treats its backwardation allowance as neutral in the long run (Ofgem backwardation deadband decision, 21 Nov 2025, para 1.5). The historical gap between the cap's forward index and outturn spot is forward prices overtaken by events, not a stable premium: measured against Elexon MID outturn it is +22.7 / +20.1 / -7.4 GBP/MWh for the 2020 cap periods and +55.0 / +23.7 / +6.7 / -7.6 for 2024, turning negative whenever prices rose; against the 12-month delivery periods the 2020 indices actually priced it averages about -4. GB forward premia reverse sign by day and season (Bunn and Chen, J. Empirical Finance 23, 2013); the CMA found no systematic bias in forward cost benchmarks (Energy Market Investigation final report, 2016, para 9.307); German baseload ex-post premia run about 3% month-ahead to 10% year-ahead (Bonaldo, Caporin and Fontini, 2021). No published 2030 GB bill projection adds a premium to modelled spot. The sensitivities span -3% to +5%, with +10% as a stress case.

retired_calibration.reason: Retired 28 Sep 2026. Fitted on 2020 cap periods compared against their own delivery quarters, but the 2020 caps used a 6-2-12 semi-annual index priced over 12-month delivery windows (Ofgem Default Tariff Cap, Appendix 6, May 2018, para 2.6), and the 2024 caps a 3-1.5-12 index averaging 12 months of observations. Both test years fell in falling markets, so the apparent 37% improvement on held-out 2024 is an artefact of the windows and the price trend, not evidence of a premium.

procurement_bridge.reference_source: Residual between the Electricity Bills 2030 direct-fuel allowance (GBP269 per 3.1 MWh) and the midpoint of its stated GBP60-80/MWh wholesale assumption. Retained only as a comparison for the decomposed allowances above.

quarter_weights.basis: Ofgem PC1 (single-rate domestic) demand share per quarter
quarter_weights.period: October 2026 - December 2026 (2026-27 Winter), the latest cap period
quarter_weights.source: Ofgem default tariff cap, Annex 2 wholesale cost allowance methodology v1.30 (26 Aug 2026), tab 3b Demand, rows 29-32 'Elec PC1', column AD; Ofgem's analysis of Elexon data (its 'Demand and Losses' workbook), updated each cap period
quarter_weights.note: User decision 6 Oct 2026: weight the quarterly base/peak blends as the cap does. The household profile has no seasonal shape, so weighting by its volume gave each quarter its share of hours (24.5% to 25.2%). On the 6 Oct run the change is -0.27 GBP/MWh on the blend, about -0.96 GBP a household with the uplifts, because this weather year's dearest quarters are Q1 and Q3 and its cheapest Q4.

shaping.source: Ofgem default tariff cap, Annex 2 wholesale cost allowance methodology v1.30 (26 Aug 2026, Q4 2026): tab 3b Demand peak 0.3 / baseload 0.7; tab 3a Allowances single-rate electricity seasonal to monthly shaping 0.232182%, monthly peak/baseload to hourly shaping 4.160818%, identical in every period from January 2019 to Q4 2026 (and in the repository's 2020 workbooks). Ofgem, Energy price cap: technical approach to MHHS, call for input, 25 Mar 2026, A1.10: 'The current shaping allowances were set in 2018', derived by converting monthly base/peak contracts to hourly using seasonal-normal PC1 demand and historical day-ahead price ratios (Default Tariff Cap decision, Nov 2018, Appendix 4, Table A4.6). Ofgem plans to reset them from supplier smart-meter data (consultation autumn 2026, decision early 2027).
shaping.rationale: The bill's domestic profile is Ofgem's two-block 70/30 allocation (55.1% of volume in the 35.8% of peak-block hours), i.e. the shape of a 70/30 contract, so the model cannot see the monthly-to-hourly step the allowance prices; its own shaping is a month and weekday effect (+0.24% over the blend). Applying Ofgem's rates is the cap rule, labelled as such, not a modelled cost. Evidence on direction: solar is eroding the GB day-ahead peak premium (ICIS, 17 Aug 2026: peak/base 1.03 in 2025 to 0.98 in 2026 to date) while the domestic evening peak remains, so the cost of reshaping 70/30 blocks is more likely to rise than fall; Ofgem says it lacks robust evidence on this (MHHS call for input, 2.83).
shaping.sensitivities_note: low_1pct approaches the model's own profile shaping; high_7pct allows for a peakier evening residual and a peak block that has lost its premium. model_profile_only is also reported.

cfd.formula: annual PyPSA CfD payment on balancing dispatch / CfD eligible GSP volume * 3.1 MWh * household loss factor, rebased to GBP real 2025
cfd.strike_basis: Published allocation-round clearing prices in 2012 prices, indexed to the 2024 model basis by cfd_strike_indexation. Rounds with several delivery-year clearing prices are collapsed to a capacity-weighted mean because a PyPSA generator carries a round label but no delivery-year vintage.
cfd.negative_price_rule_decision: none on the calibrated constraint basis (12 Oct 2026): the cal_zc3 and fin4 balancing months bid every CfD at strike minus wholesale with no negative-price exemption (contract_value_bids.negative_price_rule: none, the NESO/FTI rule chosen by the 10-11 Oct constraint calibration), and the projector refuses a bill whose rule differs from the bid audit, so this twin of 2030_pypsa_informed_assumptions.json settles the CfD line on the same rule; it is otherwise identical. The central file keeps gb_contract_terms. Previous decision: gb_contract_terms (26 Sep 2026): each round's own term, applied once the contract-aware wholesale order (scripts/market/curtailment_order.py) lets hours clear below zero. AR4 and later: no payment in any hour with a strictly negative reference price. AR2-AR3: no payment inside a run of six or more consecutive negative hours; AR1 carries no term (the rule applies to contracts offered from 1 January 2016, Explanatory Memorandum to SI 2015/1425, para 4.3; corrected 6 Oct 2026). Investment Contracts and Hinkley Point C: no negative pricing term. AR7/AR7a assumed to keep the AR4 rule. Sources: LCP 'New CfD rules - the case for further reform'; CMS 'AR4 update'; Frontier Economics 'Impact of negative pricing on renewable support'. The balancing bids apply the same rule (contract_value_bids.negative_price_rule) and record it in their audit, which the compensation reads.
cfd.negative_price_rule_note: Under the contract-aware wholesale order (decision D1, 27 Sep 2026) AR4 and later CfDs bid 0 (ar4_plus_bid_gbp_per_mwh; the earlier -1 is kept as a sensitivity), merchant renewables +0.5 (merchant_variable_cost_gbp_per_mwh) and older contracts minus their strike, so the price clears negative only when AR1-AR3, Investment Contract or HPC plant is marginal, and each round's term applies: AR4+ unpaid in any hour below zero, AR2-AR3 unpaid inside runs of six or more negative hours, AR1, Investment Contracts and HPC paid throughout. The summary reports the hours that genuinely clear below zero (hours_price_below_minus_0_01_gbp_per_mwh) and the order the saved wholesale used (wholesale_curtailment_order). The balancing bids apply the same rule and record it in their audit; the projector refuses a bill whose rule differs from the audit's. On an as-built wholesale (every CfD unit at 0) no hour clears below zero, hours bunch at or just above zero, and the rule cannot bite.

reference_price_basis.note: Intermittent CfDs settle against the hourly day-ahead reference price. Baseload CfDs such as Hinkley Point C settle against a season-ahead baseload reference price. The model has no forward market, so the season-ahead price is proxied by the demand-weighted mean wholesale price of the season the snapshot falls in (Apr-Sep summer, Oct-Mar winter), computed over the full calendar year of hourly prices and system demand. Contracts on the listed carriers use that series; every other contract settles hourly. The per-season prices applied are reported in the summary under cfd_reference_price_basis. CCS Biomass is listed because the Power BECCS CfDe uses a baseload market reference price (DESNZ GGR and Power BECCS business model update, December 2023; item MR7). Biomass is listed for its two CfD units: Drax's bridging CfD settles against a season-ahead reference, and MGT Teesside's Investment Contract is a baseload biomass CfD (item MR5); merchant biomass is unaffected.

cfd.economic_curtailment_rule_note: The copperplate wholesale LP turns CfD generators down whenever the market clears at ~GBP0, and no difference payment is booked on that energy. Contracts allocated before AR4 (AR1-AR3, the FID-enabling Investment Contracts and the Hinkley Point C contract) carry no zero-payment term, so the real generator would generate through such hours and be paid strike minus reference. With pay_pre_ar4_at_strike the projector reads the wholesale networks, takes curtailed_h = max(p_nom x p_max_pu - p_wholesale, 0) for CfD generators whose cfd_round is in pre_ar4_rounds in hours where the wholesale price is at or below zero_price_threshold_gbp_per_mwh, and adds sum(curtailed_h x hours x max(strike - price_h, 0)) to the CfD line using the same indexed strike table. Hinkley Point C has no time-varying p_max_pu in the saved network, so its availability is PyPSA's static default of 1.0. With none the payment is recorded as zero. The amount, energy, rounds and threshold are reported in the summary diagnostics. Known simplification (moot while the rule is none): Hinkley Point C's curtailed energy is valued at strike minus the hourly price, while its settled output uses the seasonal baseload reference declared in reference_price_basis (1.31 TWh of HPC energy on the last as-built year).
cfd.coverage_note: Includes CfD-tagged generators and modelled system wholesale reference prices only. It is not a forecast of the statutory supplier levy until coverage, losses and reconciliation are independently audited.
cfd.vintage_schedule_note: Allocation rounds are assigned to CP30 CfD capacity in proportion to the MW each round awarded for delivery by 2030-31. The CP30 fleet is synthetic, so this is a fleet-level vintage mix rather than site-level contract identity: a generator's round says which tranche its capacity represents, not which project it is. Takes effect only after the twelve monthly networks are rebuilt.

nuclear_exclusion.status_note: The rebuilt monthly networks place nuclear by data/market/CP30/nuclear_station_schedule_2030.csv: Hinkley Point C is labelled as a CfD (round HPC) at HINP41 at 2,317 MW (unit 1, 1,630 MW, plus unit 2 pro-rated 5/12 for its 2030-07-31 TEC date) and Sizewell B (1,198 MW) at SIZE41 is merchant and unlabelled. The HPC difference payment is therefore inside the CfD line, settled at the published HPC strike indexed from 2012 prices against the baseload reference declared in reference_price_basis. The diagnostic below (hpc_strike x modelled nuclear energy against a flat sensitivity reference) is now a cross-check on the settled payment rather than an estimate of a missing line; the settled payment itself is reported as nuclear_cfd_settled_payment_gbp and nuclear_cfd_in_bill_gbp_per_3100kwh.
nuclear_exclusion.note: CP30 publishes nuclear only as an unresolved national total for the pathway (3,515 MW and 25,892 GWh in 2030), with no station breakdown in ES1 or the N1/N2 reference sheet. The TEC register resolves it: Hinkley Point C unit 1 is effective 2029-03-31 and unit 2 2030-07-31, so 1,198 + 1,630 + 5/12 x 1,630 = 3,507 MW against CP30's 3,515 MW, and the AGR fleet is closed by 2030 (Heysham 2 and Torness, 2030-01-01). CP30 scenarios therefore place nuclear by data/market/CP30/nuclear_station_schedule_2030.csv rather than by spatial proxy: Sizewell B unsupported and Hinkley Point C on its CfD at round HPC. Sizewell B's own output stays unlabelled, which is correct - it is merchant. Nothing else in the bill covers an HPC difference payment: sizewell_c_rab is a Regulated Asset Base construction levy for a different station, and nuclear_contract_counterparty is the counterparty body's own operating cost. The diagnostic below prices an HPC-strike CfD on the modelled nuclear energy; while status is scheduled_hpc_cfd_pending_rebuild it measures the missing line, and after the rebuild it is a cross-check on the settled payment. A previous fes_cfd_fractions entry of nuclear: 1.0 justified as 'SZC' has been removed. The thermal path does apply those fractions (an earlier version of this note wrongly called the entry dead), so the removal is on principle: Sizewell C is RAB-financed rather than CfD-financed and its levy is already an explicit external line, and a fleet-wide fraction cannot express one CfD station beside one unsupported station. The station schedule does.
nuclear_exclusion.resolution: Resolved by data/market/CP30/nuclear_station_schedule_2030.csv, applied in the thermal integration by scripts/CP30/nuclear_schedule.py and declared per scenario at spatial_proxy.nuclear_station_schedule. Amend that file if CP30's nuclear assumption is later restated, then rebuild the monthly networks so the labels reach the saved dispatch.
nuclear_exclusion.hpc_strike_note: 89.50 since Sizewell C's financial close (4 Nov 2025); the published 2016 value was 92.50. Carried in data/market/lccc/cfd_strike_prices_by_round.csv itself since the 2030 re-solve (OW12, 3 Oct 2026); from 29 Sep to 3 Oct 2026 it was a bill-only strike override

cfd.ccs_levy_note: Item MR7 (user decision 23 Sep 2026): CP30's 450 MW of CCS biomass is a converted Drax unit on a Power BECCS dual CfD. Its electricity leg (CfDe) is settled like any CfD, at the declared strike of 109.90 GBP/MWh in 2012 prices (round POWER_BECCS, equal to Drax's signed bridging CfD) against a baseload reference, and booked here instead of in the CfD line. The carbon-removal leg (CfDc) is not on the electricity bill. No Power BECCS contract has been signed; this reverses item F1's sourced nil, which rested only on that, as a CP30-consistent assumption.

DRAX_BRIDGE.note: Item MR5. Drax's bridging CfD supports about 6 TWh a year across four units (a 27% load factor); CP30 converts one unit to BECCS by 2030, so the collar is prorated to three units, 4.5 TWh. Output above it is merchant. Applied pro rata to the hours each monthly settlement covers.

cfd.economic_curtailment_rule_decision: none (26 Sep 2026). The rule was built for the as-built wholesale, where every CfD unit bid 0 and pre-AR4 output was curtailed in a zero-price tie that real plant, paid through such hours, would not have accepted. The contract-aware order (market.wholesale.renewable_curtailment_order: contract_aware, scripts/market/curtailment_order.py) bids AR1-AR3, Investment Contract and Hinkley Point C units at minus their strike, so the wholesale curtails them only at a price at or below -strike, which is where the generator backs off itself; the premise no longer holds, and paying max(strike - price, 0) on that energy would pay about twice the strike for output no one would have generated. The projector reads each saved wholesale network's CfD marginal costs and refuses the rule on a contract-aware run (wholesale_curtailment_order in project_future_bill.py). pay_pre_ar4_at_strike stays available for as-built runs; on the last as-built year it added GBP 1,210M on 12.5 TWh.
cfd.strike_overrides_note: None since the 2030 re-solve (OW12, 3 Oct 2026): the HPC cut to 89.50 is in the strike table itself, which the solves and the bill both read, so the BM bids and the CfD line settle on one strike. The former override's evidence is kept below as hpc_strike_reduction.

hpc_strike_reduction.source: HPC CfD (2016): the strike falls by GBP3/MWh to 89.50 (2012 prices) if Sizewell C reaches FID (NAO, Hinkley Point C, HC 40, June 2017, timeline Figure 1 note 1 and Figure 2 note 3, https://www.nao.org.uk/wp-content/uploads/2017/06/Hinkley-Point-C.pdf; World Nuclear News, Hinkley Point C contract terms, https://www.world-nuclear-news.org/Articles/Hinkley-Point-C-contract-terms). Sizewell C FID 22 Jul 2025 and financial close 4 Nov 2025; EDF URD 2025 (2 Apr 2026) p.76-77: 'following the completion of the financing of Sizewell C on 4 November 2025, the strike price for HPC was reduced from 92.5 to 89.50 2012/MWh'

sizewell_c_offset.question_a_payment_inside_szc_rab: Yes. Sizewell C paid HPC GBP1.6bn in November 2025 for confidential cost and progress information, know-how and lessons learned (NAO, Sizewell C, 20 May 2026, para 1.13). The payment is a Sizewell C construction cost: a sunk cost in category A (Figure 5 note 2) and inside the lower and higher regulatory thresholds, though outside the Company's 38.2bn project baseline (para 1.15, Figure 4 note 3). The RAB accrues from financial close and Ofgem's nuclear RAB allowance recovers its allowed revenue, so the payment's return is inside the bill's sizewell_c_rab line, which is that allowance (Annex 4 v1.25, nRAB).
sizewell_c_offset.question_b_owners_compensated_in_full: Yes, on both parties' accounts. NAO para 1.14: 'The GBP1.6 billion payment was calculated to exactly offset the impact of the GBP3 per MWh reduction.' EDF URD 2025 p.76: the 2025 impairment is 'mainly due to a reduction in the contract for difference strike price of GBP3/MWh2012 ... this is fully offset by the payment to Hinkley Point C of GBP1.6 billion for the know-how and series effect that Sizewell C benefited from' (note 9.3: strike cut EUR1,783m of impairment against the EUR1,613m payment).
sizewell_c_offset.question_c_net_saving_to_bill_payers: Less than GBP3/MWh. Bill payers save GBP3/MWh (2012) on HPC's settled output on the CfD line, but pay the return on the GBP1.6bn payment through Sizewell C's RAB (6.73% CPIH-real regulated cost of capital, NAO Appendix One para 17), and its depreciation once Sizewell C operates. The payment was sized to offset the cut at EDF's own discount rate, which is above the RAB's, so over the life the net saving is small, and in 2030 it is negative. No netting is applied to the Sizewell C line: that line is Ofgem's actual allowance, which already carries the payment, so the model had been charging the payment without the cut; applying 89.50 removes that double charge.

sizing_2030.hpc_modelled_capacity_note: 2,317 MW (unit 1 plus unit 2 pro-rated 5/12); EDF now expects only unit 1 in 2030 (URD 2025 note 9.7: unit 2 twelve months after unit 1)
sizing_2030.note: GBP 2024: the cut is 3.00 x 1.39334 = 4.18 GBP/MWh on the settled output; the RAB return is the payment rebased with CPIH (132.9/138.0) at 6.73% a year. About 0.85 GBP a household ex VAT off the CfD line (0.60 on unit 1 alone) against about 1.10 already in the Sizewell C line.

hpc_strike_reduction.solve_side: From 29 Sep to 3 Oct 2026 this was a bill-only override and the market solves kept 92.50 (the table is a declared input of the solve rules, so editing it re-triggers every solve). For the 2030 re-solve (OW12) the table itself carries 89.50, so Stage 1 bids HPC at minus 89.50 indexed (about -125, 4.18 GBP/MWh above the old bid), which changes no dispatch that a near-zero-cost nuclear unit already runs through, and the balancing bids, the CfD curtailment compensation and the CfD line all read the same strike.

bsuos_constraints.formula: (accepted offer cost + accepted bid cost - feasibility slack - non-participant penalty turn-down + interconnector re-trading, plus CfD curtailment compensation only under add_post_hoc) / GSP charging volume * 3.1 MWh * household loss factor, rebased to GBP real 2025
bsuos_constraints.recovery_denominator: gsp_charging_volume_mwh (item F18: BSUoS is charged on BM-unit metered volume x the transmission loss multiplier) from the case recovery-demand assumptions file, at the household loss factor
bsuos_constraints.compensation_note: CfD payments are recomputed on balancing dispatch, so constrained-off CfD wind lowers the CfD line and the generator is compensated for the foregone difference payment through its balancing bid. Under reconcile_against_lp_bid (the declared treatment) the balancing LP bids each CfD unit its contract value, so that compensation is already inside the accepted bid cost; it is recomputed only to reconcile against the LP's own CfD bid cost and is not added. Under add_post_hoc (a scalar-priced LP) it is added.
bsuos_constraints.cfd_curtailment_compensation_treatment_n: add_post_hoc suits a run whose balancing LP priced CfD bids at a scalar: the compensation is genuinely absent from the accepted bid cost and is added. reconcile_against_lp_bid suits a run solved with market.balancing.renewable_support_pricing.contract_value_bids enabled, where each CfD unit bids max(strike - reference, 0) per snapshot and the settlement is already inside the accepted bid cost; the term is then recomputed only as a check against the LP's own CfD bid cost, and adding it would double count. The extraction reads each month's contract-value bid audit and refuses to run when the declaration and the solve disagree. Switch this to reconcile_against_lp_bid in the same change that adopts the contract-value re-solve.
bsuos_constraints.cfd_compensation_reconciliation_toleranc: Under reconcile_against_lp_bid the recomputed compensation and the balancing LP's own accepted CfD bid cost are the same quantity by construction, so the extraction refuses to write when they differ by more than this share of the recompute. The honest residual is the hours where a generator is turned both up and down and the LP's decrease variable is not exactly max(p_wholesale - p_balancing, 0); that measured -0.010 per cent on the one-week reinforced run (GBP -430 on GBP 4,424,648). A breach means the LP and the bill are not pricing the same contracts, which is what the old untraced GBP 4.49bn against GBP 3.96bn discrepancy would have looked like had it been checked.
bsuos_constraints.excludes: Feasibility slack (unserved load priced at VOLL) and turn-down of balancing non-participants priced at the LP's penalty bid: both sit inside the accepted offer and bid costs and are subtracted (item B8). Voltage and stability constraints are a separate NESO-outturn line.
bsuos_constraints.include_interconnector_retrading_note: NESO's constraint-management costs include the trades it makes on interconnectors to relieve constraints. The balancing model changes the interconnector schedule relative to the wholesale position and values that change at the CP30 FFR bid/ask trade prices (resources/CP30/CP30_interconnector_prices.csv). When true the amount is inside constraint_cost_gbp; it is reported separately as interconnector_retrading_cost_gbp so it can be excluded from the comparison with NESO's outturn if a narrower definition is wanted.

cp30_pathway_curtailment_twh.source: resources/CP30/CP30_ES1.csv Further Flex and Renewables 2030 Curtailment (TWh)

The floor level represents the minimum amount of annual revenue that the licensee is guaranteed to earn (provided it meets the 80% minimum availability requirement); consumers top-up revenue below this level ... also ... via the TNUoS charges process.' bsuos_other_services.method: User decision, 6 Oct 2026 (the bill's network-related lines follow the system Clean Power 2030 assumes), on the OW16 follow-up structure (3 Oct 2026, as FES 2050 decision 65). The line holds three things: NESO's internal cost and incentive, the daily trade categories and contracted ancillary services. The services, with the reserve trades the categories held, are the ancillary table's 2030 spend (GBP 1335.0 m centrally against the FY2024/25 outturn of GBP 720.8 m), the money scripts/public_ownership/support_lines_2050.py credits to the providers, in the register and outside it, so the bill and the register carry the same money. Each service is its FY2024/25 outturn carried to 2030 by a CP30 driver (scripts/public_ownership/ancillary_services_2030.py; per-row basis in the table): stability = the contracted pathfinder and mid-term book live in 2030 plus CP.21's additional short-circuit level (37,053 MVA at band midpoints) at the Phase 2 and 3 cost (GBP 8,007/MVA a year); commercial reactive = today's book plus CP.21's additional absorption and injection (6,256 Mvar) at the Voltage 2026 tender's GBP 12,848/Mvar a year; response x1.143 (4.8 / 4.2 GW) and reserve x1.455 positive, x2.167 negative (CP30 Annex 3 s.2.3.2 against NESO's 2025 need, Operability Strategy Report March 2025), at FY2024/25 prices; restoration x1.5 (ESRS); ORPS and the bilateral pumped-storage reserve held; closed services zero. The internal cost and the categories less the reserve trades stay held flat per MWh of NESO's chargeable volume, GBP 2.5275/MWh, on the 2030 GSP charging volume: CP30 gives no basis for them. Item F18 (user, 6 Oct 2026): BSUoS is a GSP-rate line, charged since April 2023 on final demand's BM-unit metered volume x the transmission loss multiplier (NESO's FY2024/25 chargeable volume, 275.15 TWh, is that volume, not metered supply), so the line is spread over the GSP charging volume and charged on the household's 3.1 MWh x the household loss factor. Covers response, reserve, reactive, restoration, stability, energy imbalance and NESO internal and contracted costs; excludes constraints, which PyPSA supplies. Low and high (the CP.21 band ends, response and reserve price and volume factors) are a named bill sensitivity (sensitivity_cost_gbp).
limitations: The services are a declared projection on CP30's drivers; NESO publishes no 2030 ancillary-services cost forecast.

Stability is priced at the Phase 2 and 3 pathfinder cost per MVA (synchronous condensers and grid-forming batteries, inertia included); the Long-term 2029 tender (stability, reactive and restoration from 2029) has not reported. At Phase 3's cost alone the stability spend would be about GBP 256 m higher; at Phase 2's about GBP 193 m lower.
CP.21 gives West Midlands and West England no values although CP30 Annex 3 names both as voltage-support areas; they count as zero, so the reactive requirement is a floor.
Contract totals are taken as 2024 money over their terms (not indexed); FY2024/25 outturn is nominal treated as 2024 money.
NESO's internal cost is held flat per MWh; its Oct-2026 forecast runs higher (about GBP 66.5 m a month).

Constraints are subtracted in full (thermal, voltage and inertia); the voltage and inertia part is carried by its own line, bsuos_voltage_and_stability_constraints, and the thermal part by the modelled redispatch.
Low and high are a named bill sensitivity; the register's support line stays on the central case.

duos.method: Base: the GB average of the 14 regions in Ofgem cap 17a (Oct-Dec 2026, DNO charging year 2026/27): nil-consumption charge GBP42.387 a year and 2,500 kWh charge GBP110.147, so a unit charge of GBP27.104/MWh and GBP126.41 at 3,100 kWh (Oct-Dec 2026 money), a clean base (zero Supplier of Last Resort and bad-debt adders). Revenue over 2026/27: FY2029/30 x1.0243, FY2030/31 x1.0412 (about 1.9% a year real in ED3, against 3.1% under the ED2 RAV growth used before). Charging base (user decision, 6 Oct 2026): the unit part of the charge (27.104/MWh x 3.1 MWh, 66.5% of the base) is spread over CP30's demand growth (ED1 row 17, GB Total System Demand minus electrolysis, by DNO charging year), so the charge per unit of revenue is x0.9552 in FY2029/30 and x0.9380 in FY2030/31; the fixed per-site part moves with revenue alone. Ofgem's Annex 3 tab 3f takes those Annex 1 fixed charges: for each of the nine regions retrieved, the 2024/25 domestic fixed charge equals the tab 3f value to the penny. So the cap DUoS includes the adders.

remaining_ccs.method: The only CCS contract charged to electricity bills by 2030 is the Net Zero Teesside Power DPA (742 MW gas CCS, signed December 2024, LCCC payments from 2028/29) through the CfD supplier levy. The plant is dispatched in the model as a committed overlay (support label DPA, outside the CfD line), but the DPA payment is not settled from model dispatch, so the payment stays an external line. No official 2030 figure exists; the ECC full business case's operating budget, which also covers Exchequer-funded T&S support, is spread over eligible supply as an upper bound. Industrial capture, T&S and hydrogen support are Exchequer- or gas-funded and add nothing.

DPA variable payments and the clawback move with power and carbon prices; the table is DESNZ's pre-FID planning figure.
Treating the EII exemption as applying to DPA costs as to CfD costs is an assumption.
Policy can change: DESNZ could move industrial or T&S support onto an electricity levy under Energy Act 2023 powers.
'Further DPA plants will not be operating by 2030' is an inference from build times, not a published statement.

battery_revenue_top_up.label: Battery revenue top-up (batteries short of their required revenue after ancillary services)
battery_revenue_top_up.source_table: cp30_2030_cp30_network register: battery_revenue_top_up_gbp on the private case
battery_revenue_top_up.method: User decision (3 Oct 2026), the FES 2050 decisions 58, 63 and 67 applied to 2030: batteries (carrier Battery) are merchant and stay short of their required revenue (capital at the private rate, O&M, generator TNUoS and insurance) after their market, Capacity Market, ancillary-service (NESO FY24/25 outturn) and declared sub-hourly revenue (+20% of wholesale plus balancing revenue), so the bill tops each battery row up to break even. Sized in the cp30_2030_cp30_network register on the private case after every other income (scripts/public_ownership/support_lines_2050.py) and read here from the run group's public account (cases.private.battery_revenue_top_up_gbp), spread over metered supply (item F18). The same payment goes to the row's owner in every market case: a state-held battery needs less at the public rate, and the difference is the state's surplus, returned to bills under the base incidence. The acquisition tariff replaces it. Long-duration storage (LAES) is on the LDES cap and floor instead.
limitations: A declared support line: no such scheme exists; it keeps the FES battery fleet whole.
Sized on the solved year's dispatch and the private case's revenue; a state owner is paid the same amount.

The wholesale and CfD lines remain sensitive to those curves in the hours interconnectors are marginal.
